era: Xbox 360 / PlayStation 3 / Wii / Nintendo DS / Mobile / PC / Modern consoles
summary: EA's analog-stick skateboarding series; use Xbox 360/backward-compatible Xbox routes for the original trilogy, Wii for Skate It, and PC for the evolving 2025 free-to-play reboot.

entries.title: Skate

emulation.emulator: Xbox backward compatibility / Xenia if compatible
emulation.notes: Prefer official Xbox backward compatibility where available.

primary.version: Original Xbox 360 release / Xbox backward compatibility
primary.why: The first Skate shipped on Xbox 360, PS3, and mobile; the Xbox 360 version has the strong original console route and later Xbox backward compatibility, while the mobile game is a distinct reduced adaptation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 version on Xbox 360 or backward-compatible Xbox hardware; use Xenia only if compatible.

secondary.exclusive_content: Mobile version has Thrasher Mode and Free Skate structured around a smaller San Vanelona adaptation.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the mobile-specific mission structure only if a preserved compatible phone build is available.
secondary.why: It is a distinct mobile adaptation rather than the main full-console game.

all_releases.fidelity: Original HD-console release, later added to Xbox backward compatibility.
all_releases.reason: primary: best preserved console route with modern Xbox compatibility.
skip: comparable HD route, but Xbox 360 has the stronger backward-compatible preservation path.

all_releases.fidelity: Mobile adaptation with Thrasher Mode, Free Skate, and a smaller level set.
all_releases.reason: secondary: play only for the mobile-specific structure.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The mobile version is a different reduced adaptation; Xbox 360 remains the full-console primary.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists; original online multiplayer was shut down in 2011.

emulation.notes: Use Dolphin with appropriate Wii input mapping; original hardware is best for Balance Board support.

primary.why: Skate It released on Wii, DS, and iOS; the Wii version has 480p/widescreen support, a deeper career, offline and online multiplayer, Balance Board support, and the first playable female skater option in the series.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Wii version on original hardware or Dolphin with Wii Remote/Nunchuk controls; use the Balance Board only if you want the novelty control route.

all_releases.fidelity: Wii release with 480p/widescreen, motion controls, Balance Board support, deeper career, and multiplayer.
all_releases.reason: primary: most complete sourced version of the spin-off.
skip: inventive handheld route, but lower fidelity and less complete than Wii.

all_releases.fidelity: Direct port of the Nintendo DS version.
all_releases.reason: skip: mobile port of the DS route, not the complete Wii version.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: DS/iOS have unique touch input but Wii has the fuller feature set and better presentation.

primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows early-access build if you want the evolving live-service version; revisit after a final release or major content-lock changes.
